rule: When cancelling or modifying an order, always check order.status === 'shipped' first and throw AppError('ORDER_ALREADY_SHIPPED') before any further logic.

evidence.quote: If the order is already shipped you need to throw here — we can't let cancellation go through on a shipped order. Should be `throw new AppError('ORDER_ALREADY_SHIPPED')`.
Same issue as PR #13 — you cannot cancel a shipped order. The guard should be at the top of this function: check status, throw `AppError('ORDER_ALREADY_SHIPPED')` immediately.
Shipped orders are final. Any attempt to modify or cancel must throw `AppError('ORDER_ALREADY_SHIPPED')` — we've reverted this twice already, please add a test to lock it in.

rule: Always call audit.record(eventName, data) — never audit.log(). The data object must include orderId, and eventName must follow the pattern 'order.<verb>'.

evidence.quote: We're calling `audit.log(...)` but that method doesn't exist. The module only exposes `audit.record(eventName, data)`. This will blow up at runtime.
Still using `audit.log` — this doesn't exist. Switch to `audit.record('order.cancelled', { orderId: order.id })`. Event names are `order.<verb>` and data must include `orderId`.
`audit.record` takes `(eventName, data)` where data must have `orderId`. Something like `audit.record('order.refunded', { orderId: order.id, amountCents })`. There's no `audit.log`.
TypeError: audit.log is not a function
Fix audit calls to use audit.record with correct event names (#25)

rule: Always use clock.now() for all timestamps — never Date.now(). The clock module is injected specifically to allow time to be frozen in tests.

evidence.quote: Use `clock.now()` here instead of `Date.now()`. The whole point of injecting the clock is so tests can freeze time — `Date.now()` breaks that.
`clock.now()` please, not `Date.now()`. We've had this conversation before — see PR #14.
Switch remaining Date.now() calls to clock.now() (#18)

rule: Issue all refunds via payments.refund(order.paymentRef, amountCents). Never read from or write to total_cents directly to perform a refund.

evidence.quote: Refunds have to go through `payments.refund(order.paymentRef, amountCents)`. Don't touch `total_cents` directly — invoicing reads that field and any mutation will corrupt the invoice.
You're zeroing out `total_cents` again. Don't do this — invoicing reads it directly. Issue the refund via `payments.refund(order.paymentRef, amountCents)` and leave `total_cents` alone.
Revert "Refund by zeroing total_cents" - broke invoicing (#23)
Issue refunds via payments.refund, remove direct total_cents mutation (#17)

rule: Use Math.floor (not Math.round) when calculating partial refund amounts in cents. Math.round can produce a 1-cent over-refund that causes reconciliation failures.

evidence.quote: Be careful with rounding on partial refunds — floating point here can bite you.
To be precise on the rounding: use `Math.floor`, never `Math.round`. Even 1 cent over-refund is a real-money error that will cause reconciliation failures.
Apply Math.floor for partial refund amount calculation (#22)
